title: Grateful Dead Live at Roosevelt Stadium on 1972-07-18
lineage: AUD MC> ?> R> D> SHN> CDR, with change to A:MC> ?> C> D source toward end

ai_review.summary: Audience tape of the 7/18/72 show captures a high‑energy Dark Star and a gorgeous Truckin’→Dark Star transition, with generally listenable sound despite some harsh stadium bleed.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its explosive Dark Star, powerful “Truckin' → Dark Star” segue and memorable Pigpen moments, delivering the classic ’72 vibe that many fans remember. The audience recording isn’t pristine – there’s noticeable stadium boom and occasional drop‑outs – but it remains listenable and conveys the concert’s excitement.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (8 of 10) give 4–5 stars, highlighting strong musical moments and deeming the tape listenable; only a few note serious sound issues, leading to an overall high rating with strong confidence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally listenable audience recording; some reviewers mention harsh stadium boom, off‑key tape resonance and occasional drop‑outs, but low/high ends are praised when boosted.

standout_songs: Pigpen’s soulful two‑minute piece (referenced as “Two Souls”)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is remembered for its seamless, high‑energy flow especially in the second set where Dark Star expands and flows into Comes A Time; overall pacing is described as strong despite a few rough moments.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals noted as strong at this point; guitar tone not specifically mentioned but overall performance praised.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (on keyboards) called “quite incredible”, blowing away Keith and delivering superb playing.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy’s drumming likened to Tony Williams, providing a powerful, jazzy drive.
